RNA-seq data for prokaryotes can be improved by accounting for operon structure.

1) RNA sequencing of polycistronic operons can lead to reads that span multiple genes; 2) existing RNA seq analysis tools are not optimized for prokaryotes; and 3) FADU, our tool that accounts for operonic gene structure, can significantly improve the quantification of prokaryote RNA seq data.

FADU is a tool that can improve read quantification and gene expression analysis of prokaryote RNA sequencing data, and that this is achieved through the integration of prokaryotespecific strategies into existing RNA sequencing tools.

we demonstrate that the operon structure of prokaryotes is not well accounted for in the current generation of RNA seq tools and that a simple correction improves the quantification of prokaryote RNA seq.

The main takeaway from our work is that
the operon structure of the prokaryotic genome is a major source of bias for RNA sequencing data analysis.
prokaryotic gene structure must be considered when quantifying RNA seq data.
the computational analysis of prokaryote RNA seq data requires a different strategy than that for eukaryotic RNA seq data.
